## Serial consoles

- New serial session type (File › New Serial Session…) for switches, routers and other gear with a console port. Choose the port, speed, data bits, parity, stop bits and flow control; the default is 9600 8N1.
- Ports are listed by device name, such as "COM5 — USB Serial Device".
- Send Break holds the line for 300 ms, for things like breaking into ROMMON.
- Unplugging the adapter disconnects the tab with a clear message, and it reconnects when the port comes back.
- Quick connect understands `serial COM5` and `serial COM5 115200 7E1`, and PuTTY serial sessions import.

## Safe paste

- A paste that would press Enter asks first, names the session and previews the lines. It defaults to Cancel. It doesn't ask when the program on the other end handles pastes safely itself (bracketed paste), and it can be turned off in Settings › Terminal.
- For devices that drop characters, a session can wait after each line or character while pasting. Progress shows in the status bar, any key stops the paste, and Esc stops it without sending the rest.

## SSH algorithms

- Settings › Identities & Keys › SSH algorithms lets you turn individual key exchange, cipher, MAC and host key algorithms on or off. Legacy ones are marked, with a button to turn them all off.
- A session's new Advanced tab can override this for that host. Shell integration settings moved there too.
- `KexAlgorithms`, `Ciphers`, `MACs` and `HostKeyAlgorithms` in `~/.ssh/config` import as the same choices.
- The status bar tooltip shows what each connection negotiated, and the status line says when legacy algorithms are in use.

## Fixes

- No more false "host key changed" warning for RSA hosts. Trust now compares the key itself, not the name of the signature type the server offered.
- Connections offer the host key type you already trust first, as OpenSSH does.

## Easier splits

- Split dividers can be grabbed across 8 pixels instead of 1, so you no longer have to line the mouse up exactly. This applies to the sessions pane, split tabs and the file pane.
- A divider lights up after the mouse rests on it for a moment, and at once when pressed, so moving the mouse across it no longer flashes it. A lit divider is thicker and easier to see.
- The annotations ruler beside the terminal no longer has an edge line that looked like another split. It is now a faintly lighter strip. High Contrast keeps the line.

## Agents

- Tabs now recognise twenty more coding agents, each with its own icon: Aider, Amp, Antigravity, Cline, Crush, Cursor Agent, Devin, Factory Droid, GitHub Copilot, Goose, Hermes Agent, Kilo Code, Kimi Code, Kiro, Letta Code, Maki, MastraCode, Muse, Qoder and Qwen Code.

Choose the x64 download for Intel or AMD PCs. Choose ARM64 only for Windows on ARM devices.
